proposedOverrides.name: Nova Scotia peninsula (British rule)
proposedOverrides.summary: Britain governed peninsular Nova Scotia after 1713, within a region already home to Mi’kmaq communities and Acadian settlements.

identityAssessment.finding: The imported 1783 and 1800 polygons cover the Nova Scotia peninsula, with bounds approximately 66.19 to 60.96 degrees west and 43.52 to 46.05 degrees north. They do not depict the modern Acadian Peninsula in northeastern New Brunswick. The display name is clarified through overrides; no polygon or interval is changed. Historical coverage is inferred from inspected location and the cited colonial chronology, not from the imported summary.
